storage: Store in a corrosives cabinet away from alkalis.

Once bottles are opened, hydrogen chloride gas can leak out into the store and accelerate metal corrosion.
Firmly close bottles after use. Older bottles of acid may not be the expected concentration.
• Hydrogen chloride gas can also diffuse through plastic; labels on containers will fade and eventually
disintegrate. Containers themselves may become damaged and/or the acid darkens over time. Check the
state of containers, lids and labels on a regular basis. If required, decant solutions into fresh containers.
• Hydrogen chloride gas reacts with ammonia and amines. A white powder (chloride salts) will deposit on
bottles and elsewhere in the chemical store indicating (i) leaking bottles or lids (ii) acid or ammonia/amine
vapours diffusing through plastic bottles (iii) inadequate ventilation in the store.

first_aid.eyes: Rinse cautiously with water for at least 15 minutes.
first_aid.skin: Remove contaminated clothing and wash with plenty of water.

cleapss_text: Hydrochloric acid is corrosive and can cause severe skin burns and eye damage. Wear appropriate PPE. Store separately from incompatible materials.

storage: Store in a cool, dry place away from acids.

cleapss_text: Sodium hydroxide causes severe burns. Avoid contact with skin and eyes. Wear protective gloves and eye protection.

storage: Keep away from heat, sparks and open flames.

first_aid.ingestion: Seek medical advice if large quantities are swallowed.

cleapss_text: Ethanol is a highly flammable liquid and vapour. Keep containers tightly closed and away from ignition sources.
